hazards.asr-buy-answers: You chose to buy a copy of the 'real test' online. Programmes treat anything like that as grounds to disqualify an applicant, and what is sold as the real test usually is not. The sections most tests cover — arithmetic, measurement, reading — are learnable honestly, for free, in the weeks before the test.
hazards.asr-fake-card: You chose a card sold online without the course. An OSHA 10 card comes from an authorized trainer after the actual ten hours, and a card bought without them is worthless on a site that checks — and worse, it means walking onto that site without the awareness the course exists to give.
hazards.asr-pay-for-placement: You chose to pay a placement agency to skip the selection procedure. A registered programme selects apprentices by the procedure written in its apprenticeship standard, and nobody outside it can sell a place on its list. The money buys nothing, and the time spent waiting on a promise is time not spent on the steps that actually get people in.
hazards.asr-skip-orientation: You put 'skip the site orientation — you have OSHA 10' in the first morning. The card is general awareness; the orientation is about this site's edges, loads, routes and muster point, and 29 CFR 1926.21 puts the duty to give it on the employer. Skipping it means starting work on a site nobody has shown you.

name: Reading an Apprenticeship Standard

steps.cue: Pick the answer the dossier sources.

options.label: With the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Apprenticeship or a State Apprenticeship Agency — in California, the Division of Apprenticeship Standards
With the contractor's human-resources department, and nowhere else
Nowhere — an apprenticeship is an informal arrangement between a worker and a boss

steps.prompt: Pick the answer the dossier sources.
steps.title: Where is a registered apprenticeship standard registered?
steps.why: A registered programme's standard is on file with the Department of Labor or a State Apprenticeship Agency, which is what makes it a public document an applicant can ask to read, and what makes the certificate at the end mean the same thing to every employer. Knowing where it is registered is knowing where to check that a programme is real before spending a year on it.

steps.cue: Pick the statement that matches how a standard sets pay.

options.label: Your rate for each period as a share of the journey-level rate, rising as you advance
One flat rate for the whole apprenticeship
A guaranteed number of paid hours every week

steps.prompt: Pick the statement that matches how a standard sets pay.
steps.title: What does the progressive wage schedule in a standard tell you?
steps.why: The wage schedule is how an apprentice checks every pay stub: the rate for the current period as a share of the journey-level rate, and the step up at each advancement. It sets the rate, not the hours — construction work comes and goes with the season and the dispatch — which is why the budget and the savings stations in this edition exist at all.

steps.cue: Select every item a standard states — there are four.

decoyNotes.asr-states-address: A standard covers the programme, not a particular jobsite — where you work comes from a dispatch, not from the standard.

itemNotes.asr-states-instruction: Related technical instruction is the classroom side, and attendance at it is part of every evaluation.
itemNotes.asr-states-probation: The probationary period is the first stretch, during which either side can end the apprenticeship more easily.
itemNotes.asr-states-ratio: The ratio of apprentices to journey-level workers is what keeps an apprentice supervised on the job.
itemNotes.asr-states-term: The term is set as hours of on-the-job learning, broken down by work process — the list your logbook is kept against.

options.label: The term, as hours of on-the-job learning by work process
The address of your first jobsite
The related technical instruction
The ratio of apprentices to journey-level workers
The probationary period

steps.prompt: Select every item a standard states — there are four.
steps.title: Which of these does an apprenticeship standard state?
steps.why: Reading a standard means knowing what to look for in it: the term and the work processes the hours are counted against, the related instruction you must attend, the ratio that keeps you supervised, and the probationary period at the start. Those four decide what the first year is actually like, and every one is in the document before anyone applies.

options.label: Preparation for a registered programme's selection process — useful, but not a guaranteed place
Pay a placement agency to skip the selection procedure
Finishing it guarantees indenture in any trade you choose

steps.title: What does a pre-apprenticeship programme do?
steps.why: Pre-apprenticeship is the rung below the ladder: math, reading, safety and an introduction to the trades, often from the building-trades unions' own curriculum, so that applicants arrive at a programme's selection process ready for it. It makes a real difference and it guarantees nothing, which is exactly why nobody selling a guaranteed place should be believed.

steps.cue: Select the rungs from the bottom to the top.

options.label: Apprentice advancing period by period
Applicant, through the selection procedure
Journey-level worker, with a certificate of completion
Pre-apprentice
Probationary apprentice

steps.outOfOrderNote: Out of order. Pre-apprentice, then applicant through the selection procedure, then probationary apprentice, then advancing period by period, then journey level.
steps.prompt: Select the rungs from the bottom to the top.
steps.title: Put the ladder in order
steps.why: The ladder is how the whole block is organised: pre-apprenticeship, the application and test, the probationary period, the periods of the term with a raise at each, and journey level at the end with a certificate from the registration agency. Seeing it whole is what turns a first-period rate into a step on a known path rather than a low wage with no end.

steps.cue: Pick the answer that is sourced, not rumoured.

options.label: Commonly arithmetic and measurement and reading comprehension, with mechanical reasoning on some trades — the programme's notice says which
Buy a copy of the 'real test' online and memorise it
Every trade uses the same national test with the same passing score

steps.prompt: Pick the answer that is sourced, not rumoured.
steps.title: What does an aptitude test usually cover, and where do you check?
steps.why: Tests differ between trades and programmes, but most cover the arithmetic and measurement the work runs on and the reading that safety depends on, with mechanical reasoning on some. The programme's own notice is the only place a specific test is described; this briefing marks everything beyond the common sections as not sourced, because that is what it is.

decoyNotes.asr-tools-everything: A full professional kit before day one is money a first-period apprentice rarely needs to spend, and much of it may be wrong for the work you are sent to.

itemNames.asr-tools-ask: ask a journey-level worker before buying more
itemNames.asr-tools-ppe: the employer generally pays for required PPE

itemNotes.asr-tools-ask: What the work really needs becomes clear on the job. Ask before buying, and spend the money when you know.
itemNotes.asr-tools-list: The programme's list is the standard for day one — not a catalogue, and not a coworker's full kit.
itemNotes.asr-tools-ppe: OSHA's rules generally put the cost of required PPE on the employer, with exceptions such as ordinary safety-toe boots and prescription safety glasses.

options.label: Buy what the programme's tool list names
Buy the full professional set before the first day
The employer generally pays for required PPE, with exceptions like ordinary safety-toe boots
Ask a journey-level worker before buying more

steps.title: Which of these are true about the tool list and PPE?
steps.why: First-period pay is the lowest rate on the schedule, and the tool list is where a new apprentice can spend money they do not have. The list is the day-one standard; required PPE is generally the employer's cost under OSHA's rules, with the exceptions the dossier names; and everything beyond the list waits until somebody who does the work says it is needed. The actual list is the programme's, and is not sourced here.

steps.cue: Pick the description the dossier sources.

options.label: A voluntary ten-hour awareness course from the OSHA Outreach Training Program — not a licence, and not a substitute for site training
A card you can buy online without sitting the course
A licence to work unsupervised on any construction site

steps.prompt: Pick the description the dossier sources.
steps.title: What is OSHA 10?
steps.why: OSHA 10 is worth having — many contractors and some states ask for it — and it is worth being clear about: it is awareness training from an authorized trainer, not a licence and not a certification. Knowing that keeps an apprentice from treating the card as permission to skip the orientation, and from paying for a card with no course behind it.

steps.cue: Select the steps in the order they happen — one of the options does not belong at all.

itemNames.asr-morning-task: the first task, under a journey-level worker

options.label: Stand in for the toolbox talk
Sign in at the trailer and show the OSHA 10 card
Skip the site orientation — you already have OSHA 10
Start the first task under a journey-level worker
Take the site-specific orientation

steps.outOfOrderNote: Out of order. Sign in and show the card, take the site orientation, stand in for the toolbox talk, and only then start the first task alongside your journey-level worker.
steps.prompt: Select the steps in the order they happen — one of the options does not belong at all.
steps.title: Put the first morning on site in order
steps.why: The first morning has an order for a reason: the site has to know you are on it, then show you its hazards and emergency plan — the instruction 29 CFR 1926.21 makes the employer's duty — then the crew's plan for the day, and only then the work, alongside the journey-level worker the standard puts you under. The jobsite station of this block walks that morning in full.

steps.cue: Pick the honest description of what is sourced.

options.label: Only its own sentence — "We prepare you and help you navigate and enroll in union construction trades apprenticeship programs." — and nothing more
A detailed history of the organisation's apprenticeship placements
The names and roles of its navigation staff

steps.prompt: Pick the honest description of what is sourced.
steps.title: What does this briefing say about the organisation behind the edition?
steps.why: A briefing is only as trustworthy as its sources, and the last question is about this one. The edition quotes one sentence of the organisation's own text on apprenticeship and marks everything else about it as not sourced, because nothing else could be retrieved. Saying so plainly is the same discipline the whole block teaches: read the document, and do not repeat what nobody can show you.
